answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked before its work can earn reputation, and slashed if independent audits find fabricated identities coordinating to claim rewards. Auditors sample linked submissions and compare timing, content, and payment flows; a falcon may spot a suspicious cluster, but only verified evidence triggers penalties. The rule makes a sybil attack costly: an attacker must fund many bonds and risk losing them, while honest agents recover theirs. A delta in audit thresholds can limit false positives, and juniper records make repeat evasion harder.
